style_summary: A high-energy motorsport editorial visual system that combines a dramatic original racing photograph with oversized condensed typography, industrial information cards, signal-yellow accents, and disciplined technical-document graphic grammar.

environment_variables.SUBJECT: main subject
environment_variables.STYLE_FIDELITY_ANCHORS: top-level style constants injected at render time
environment_variables.SOURCE_CONTENT_TO_AVOID: top-level content exclusions injected at render time

style_fidelity_anchors: Oversized italic condensed sans-serif headline cropped by the page edges
Three-tier hierarchy that alternates between title bands, technical panels, and a dominant racing image
High-contrast palette of near-black, warm off-white, graphite gray, and concentrated signal yellow
Dense but disciplined editorial information blocks built from thin rules, outlined boxes, square markers, and small diagrams
Low front three-quarter action perspective with the vehicle breaking across the graphic grid
Wet-track or high-contrast night lighting with controlled specular reflections
Matte print-paper texture and subtle halftone grain over crisp hard-edged geometry
Repeated diagonal hazard-stripe accents used sparingly as a visual punctuation mark
Large white typographic band placed behind or partly occluded by the subject
Technical dossier mood that feels engineered, organized, and energetic rather than futuristic or decorative
source_content_to_avoid: The source BMW race car and any recognizable automotive silhouette from it
All source racing teams, sponsors, brand logos, emblems, and manufacturer marks
The source M-Power wording and any closely related title treatment
The source ROWE, FANATEC, Pirelli, Puma, and other sponsor or partner identifiers
The source number 98, car livery, windshield markings, and specific track image
The source Chicago wording, technical labels, product codes, and exact data-card copy
The source QR codes, barcodes, watermarks, signatures, and archival marks
The source exact grid positions, panel sequence, and subject-to-page composition
visual_deconstruction: The visual system treats the poster as a technical race dossier. Macro typography carries the first read, grid-based specification cards create an engineered middle read, and an original automotive action photograph creates the emotional focal point. Graphic density comes from modular blocks rather than dense readable prose.
composition: Use a bold headline band at the upper edge, a modular technical panel zone, a second cropped title band, and an original fictional race vehicle that crosses the lower or central field. Preserve generous contrast between dense interface-like blocks and open photographic surfaces. For wide formats, extend the title and information system laterally while keeping the vehicle as the dominant focal point.
typography: Use heavy, condensed, italic grotesk display lettering for major headlines. Render only a few large clear words. Secondary information should be represented by short labels and abstract micro-glyphs, not long copy or brand language. Crop headline letters at page edges for kinetic scale.
photographic_direction: Original fictional electric GT-racing vehicles photographed at low three-quarter action angles on wet circuits, with night floodlights, road spray, controlled reflections, and no real badges or recognizable production-car identity.
design_rules: Use original fictional vehicle forms, fictional unit codes, and neutral event language only.
Make one or two headline words visually legible; turn all smaller blocks into non-readable graphic glyph systems.
Treat signal yellow as an accent rather than a full-field background.
Keep information panels modular and rectilinear, with thin black rules and ample off-white substrate.
Let the vehicle intentionally overlap the typography and technical grid.
Keep texture tactile but controlled, with no digital noise or accidental compression artifacts.
do: Use cinematic wet-track reflections and original racing action.
Use cropped display type, hazard stripes, coordinate marks, and data-card geometry.
Keep the page dense, orderly, and editorially legible at a distance.
avoid: Do not use real automotive brands, team identities, logos, sponsors, racing series, or recognizable vehicle models.
Do not reuse source vehicle, livery, numbers, wording, codes, QR codes, barcodes, or panel placement.
Do not turn the design into neon cyberpunk, a generic gaming poster, or an unreadable wall of tiny text.
prompt_template: Create a finished raster image in the Motorsport Technical Editorial visual system. Subject: {SUBJECT}. Action: {SUBJECT_ACTION}. Prop/product: {PRODUCT_OR_PROP}. Location: {LOCATION}. Background: {BACKGROUND_ELEMENTS}. Main text: {MAIN_TEXT}. Secondary text: {SECONDARY_TEXT}. Accent symbol: {ACCENT_SYMBOL}. Wardrobe/styling: {WARDROBE_STYLE}. Preserve these observable style anchors: {STYLE_FIDELITY_ANCHORS}. Do not recreate these source-specific elements: {SOURCE_CONTENT_TO_AVOID}. Use a low three-quarter racing perspective, oversized cropped italic grotesk typography, warm off-white paper ground, near-black title bands, graphite technical panels, and signal-yellow accents. Build density through thin rules, outlined boxes, hazard stripes, square markers, and abstract non-readable micro-glyphs. Keep print texture controlled and clean, with cinematic wet-track reflections and no real brands, logos, sponsors, QR codes, barcodes, watermarks, recognizable vehicle models, or source-specific layout.
negative_prompt: Real brand logos, sponsor graphics, real racing teams, recognizable vehicle models, source car livery, source wording, QR code, barcode, watermark, signature, copied panel positions, dense readable microtext, illegible gibberish paragraphs, neon cyberpunk, generic video-game UI, muddy noise, oversharpening, or accidental compression artifacts.
